question: When was the first broadcasted domestic women's match in South Africa?

question: "Warriors" is the current name for which former provincial union?
explanation: Eastern Province was rebranded Warriors.

question: "Badgers" is the current name for which former provincial union?
explanation: South Western Districts was rebranded Badgers.

question: "Tuskers" is the current name for which former provincial union?

question: "Lions" is the current name for which former provincial union?
explanation: Both Central Gauteng and Gauteng were folded into the Lions.

question: "Knights" is the current name for which former provincial union?
explanation: Free State was rebranded Knights.

question: "Titans" is the current name for which former provincial union?
explanation: Northerns was rebranded Titans.

question: St George's Park hosted South Africa Women's first-ever Test in December 1960. How many years passed before it hosted its first women's ODI?
explanation: St George's Park didn't host a Women's ODI until South Africa played Ireland there in December 2025, 65 years later, making it the last of South Africa's major Test venues to do so.

question: This database's Partnership_By_Wicket records include a 151-run 7th-wicket stand from October 2024, involving Fay Cowling and one other player. That other player is a two-time World Championship medallist and an Olympic silver medallist. In which sport?
explanation: That's Sunette Viljoen-Louw, an Olympic silver medallist (Rio 2016) and two-time World Championship medallist in javelin, who returned to domestic cricket over 20 years after her only Test cap.

question: "Eastern Storm" is the current name for which former provincial union?
explanation: Easterns was rebranded Eastern Storm (not to be confused with Eastern Province, who became the Warriors).

question: Which of these players is tied for the most provincial unions represented in a career in this database, having played for five?
explanation: Janse van Rensburg played for Dolphins, Dragons, Eastern Storm, Knights and Limpopo Lillies, five unions. She's tied for the database record alongside Zizipho Mdebuka, Bernadine Bezuidenhout and Alysia Rudolph.

question: Shabnim Ismail's first and most recent appearances in this database are separated by roughly how many years?
explanation: Ismail debuted in October 2005 and was still playing as recently as March 2026, just over 20 years apart.

question: Which bowler holds the second-most 5-wicket hauls in this database's history (9), and was still playing in the 2025/26 season, over 20 years after her database debut?
explanation: Jana Nell has taken 9 five-wicket hauls across 190 matches (2005 to 2026), second only to Susan Benade's 11.

question: Which team has finished runner-up more times than any other in this database (7), despite winning the title only twice in that span?
explanation: Lions finished runner-up 7 times across List A and T20 Division 1 between 2012/13 and 2025/26, but won the title only twice.

question: Which player has scored the most double centuries (200+) in this database's history, with two?
explanation: Benade is the only player with two double centuries in this database. Four others (van Niekerk, du Preez, Thomson and Dinesha Devnarain) have one each, six double centuries in total across the database's history.

question: Which player is the only one in this database's history to score 200+ runs AND take 3+ wickets in the same match?
explanation: Susan Benade is the sole member of the 200-run/3-wicket club, achieving it in a single match against Kei on 10 February 2018 (212 runs, 3 for 26).

question: Which player is the only one to ever score 150+ runs and take 5+ wickets in a single match?
explanation: Marizanne Kapp is the only player in the database to combine a 150+ score with a 5-wicket haul in the same innings, doing so against Kei on 16 January 2011 (163 runs, 6 for 6).

question: Sune Luus is the only player to ever score 150+ runs and take 4+ wickets in the same match. Against which opposition did she achieve it, in November 2013?
explanation: Luus scored 150 and took 4 for 1 against Limpopo Lillies on 23 November 2013, the only time this double has ever been achieved.

question: Which of these teams has never finished in the top 3 (champion, runner-up, or 3rd place) across this database's 20-year history?
explanation: Warriors are one of 8 unions never to have finished in the top 3, alongside Badgers, Heat, Limpopo Lillies, Rhinos, Tuskers, Eastern Storm and Kei.

question: Excluding Western Province, which team has won the most domestic titles in this database?
explanation: Dragons have won 4 titles, the most of any union other than the dominant Western Province.

question: Ayabonga Khaka has played 95 List A matches for South African provincial sides. How many T20 matches has she played, per this database?
explanation: Khaka's List A to T20 ratio (95 to 19, roughly 5 to 1) is far more lopsided than most of her national teammates, several of whom sit closer to 1.5 to 1.

question: South Africa Women played their first ODI in August 1997, 25 years after their last Test before an extended absence from international cricket. Who was the opponent, and where was it played?
explanation: South Africa's first ODI after readmission to international cricket was against Ireland at Stormont, Belfast, on 5 August 1997.

question: Where did South Africa Women play their first-ever T20I, in August 2007?
explanation: South Africa's first women's T20I was against New Zealand at the County Ground, Taunton, on 10 August 2007, a neutral venue in England.

question: South Africa Women have only ever won one Test match in their history. Who was the opponent, and in what year?
explanation: South Africa's sole Test victory came against the Netherlands in 2007, the only Test the two sides have ever played against each other.

question: It took South Africa Women 23 attempts before they finally beat Australia for the first time in any format. When did that first win come?
explanation: South Africa beat Australia for the first time in a T20I at Manuka Oval, Canberra, on 28 January 2024, having lost 22 of the previous 23 meetings and tied one, in 2016.

question: What is South Africa Women's best-ever finish at a Cricket World Cup, achieved for the first time in 2025?
explanation: South Africa reached their first-ever Women's World Cup final in 2025, finishing runners-up to India.

question: South Africa Women won the Women's World Cup Qualifier the very first time they entered it. In what year?
explanation: South Africa won the Women's World Cup Qualifier in 2008, their first appearance in the event, and it remains their best result in it.

question: Which South African bowler took the first-ever hat-trick in the history of the ICC Under-19 Women's T20 World Cup, in 2023?
explanation: Landsman, then 18, took the first hat-trick in U19 Women's T20 World Cup history against Scotland in 2023.

question: This South African is one of only two bowlers in women's international cricket history to have taken two separate hat-tricks, her second coming against Sri Lanka in May 2025. Who is she?
explanation: Tryon joins Australia's Megan Schutt as the only players to take two hat-tricks in women's international cricket.

question: Marizanne Kapp became the all-time leading wicket-taker in Women's ODI World Cup history in 2025, surpassing which bowler's long-standing record of 43?
explanation: Kapp took her 44th World Cup wicket during South Africa's 2025 semi-final win over England, surpassing India's Jhulan Goswami.

question: Laura Wolvaardt became the first South African woman to reach 5,000 ODI runs. In how many innings did she reach the milestone, the second-fastest ever?
explanation: Wolvaardt reached 5,000 ODI runs in 117 innings, second only to India's Smriti Mandhana (112 innings).

question: Who scored South Africa Women's first-ever Test century, an unbeaten 105 against England in Cape Town in 1961?
explanation: Van Mentz's record stood for over 60 years until Marizanne Kapp passed it with 150 against England in 2022.

question: Who scored South Africa Women's first-ever ODI century, 101 not out against Ireland in December 2000?
explanation: Olivier's century came during South Africa's early years back in international cricket after readmission in 1997.

question: Who scored the first century by a South African woman at a Women's T20 World Cup, 101 off 60 balls against Thailand in 2020?
explanation: Lee's century, sharing a 131-run stand with Sune Luus, helped South Africa to a big win at the 2020 tournament in Australia.

question: Who was the first South African woman to take a five-wicket haul in a T20I, achieving the feat before Shabnim Ismail became the second in 2018?
explanation: Ismail's 5 for 30 against India in February 2018 made her the second South African to take a T20I five-wicket haul, after Sune Luus.

question: Who took South Africa Women's first-ever ODI five-wicket haul, with remarkable figures of 5 for 7 against Pakistan in February 2008?
explanation: Smith took 5 for 7 in 8 overs against Pakistan at Stellenbosch on 24 February 2008, South Africa's first ODI five-wicket haul.

question: Who took South Africa Women's first-ever Test five-wicket haul, against England at Durban on 31 December 1960, just weeks after the team's very first Test?
explanation: McNaughton took 6 wickets against England in South Africa's second-ever Test, weeks after their debut.

question: Which South African bowler has taken the most Test five-wicket hauls in history, with three, all against England or New Zealand in the early 1960s and 1972?
explanation: Ward took five-wicket hauls in January 1961 and twice more in 1972, more than any other South African in Test history.

question: Nonkululeko Mlaba took a Test five-wicket haul in South Africa's most recent Test, played in December 2024. Who were the opponents?
explanation: Mlaba took 6 for 67 against England at Mangaung Oval, Bloemfontein, South Africa's only Test since 2007.

question: Nonkululeko Mlaba is the only South African woman to ever take a 10-wicket match haul in Test cricket. What were her match figures, against England in December 2024?
explanation: Mlaba took 4 for 90 and 6 for 67 (10 for 157 in the match) against England at Bloemfontein in December 2024, the best match figures by a South African woman in Test history.
